hero.h1: Close the loop between the order and the line.
hero.dek: The ERP sends the production order; SOP runs it on the line and sends back what was made, what was used, what stopped and what was repaired, with a signed record.
hero.alt: the end of a packaging line, cases on the rollers, the day's schedule on a tablet

sections.title: The ERP sends the order, SOP runs it
sections.alt: a wall monitor with a synoptic and an open paper logbook on the desk beside it

sections.title: The loop, in one line.
cols: Who this page is for — mid-market and regional ERP vendors and their implementation partners, the ones factories already run finance and orders on.
What the shop floor asks for — execution, consumption, meters, maintenance and the record.
The loop — the ERP sends the production order; SOP runs it on the line and sends back what was made, what was used, what stopped and what was repaired, with a signed record.

sections.title: What comes back: made, used, stopped, repaired — signed
sections.alt: a standing desk at the edge of the hall, the shift handover signed on paper
sections.promise: What was made, what was used, what stopped and what was repaired — with a signed record.

sections.title: What comes back.
cols: Orders and batches — EMS orders and batches, with made and used per batch.
The parts-store ledger — what moved off the shelf, against which job.
Work orders — with labour and parts priced.
Reports over an order — the record, computed and signed over the order itself.
The seam — order, material, stock-movement and work-order interfaces.
These are what can be shown today, on the running plant.

sections.title: Inside your own contract
sections.alt: four people around a laptop on a stainless table at the end of a packaging line

sections.title: What a partnership would have to settle.
cols: Per line, inside your own contract — per-line bundles you can price inside your own contracts.
The decision we are after — add SOP as the plant-floor module of your offer.
Who owns the master data — materials, products and units: the ERP, or SOP. Settled once, per plant.
Which market first — which ERP, in which region, fits first.
Resell, or refer — both shapes are open, and settled in the conversation.

sections.title: Joint reference plants
sections.alt: a meeting room at dusk, a wall screen with five plant tiles, five people seen from behind

sections.title: Where it goes together.
cols: Joint reference plants — the plants where the loop is closed once, and both offers can point at it.
No plant is named — none exists yet to name, and none would be named.

sections.title: Write to us.
sections.alt: an engineer at an open cabinet noting the controllers on the line
sections.text: Start with one word so it reaches the right desk: DESKS. Tell us the country, what the line or machine produces, and which controllers are already on it. We reply from a person, never a queue.
